pr_title: rand: fix seeding from a weak entropy source
pr_body:
The 'rand_generate' method is not well suited for being used with
weak entropy sources in the 'get_entropy' callback, because the
caller needs to provide a preallocated buffer without knowing
how much bytes are actually needed to collect the required entropy.

Instead we use the 'rand_get_seed' and 'rand_clear_seed' methods
which were exactly designed for this purpose: it's the callee who
allocates and fills the buffer, and finally cleans it up again.

The 'rand_get_seed' and 'rand_clear_seed' methods are currently
optional for a provided random generator. We could fall back to
using 'rand_generate' if those methods are not implemented.
However, imo it would be better to simply make them an officially
documented requirement for seed sources.

Fixes #22332

@paulidale I believe that you are missing an important point:  I claim that every existing seed source which gets installed via `RAND_set_seed_source_type()` **must** already have the **get_entropy** callbacks implemented, otherwise it would be fundamentally broken:

That's because the seed source eventually gets instantiated as the parent of the main drbg:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/b6eb95fa4439ea6254a5330487dabb2a499fb6c8/crypto/rand/rand_lib.c#L734-L736

Which means that in `get_entropy()` callback the `drbg->parent != NULL` case  holds for the main drbg, so `drbg->parent_get_seed()` is used instead of the upcall:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/b6eb95fa4439ea6254a5330487dabb2a499fb6c8/providers/implementations/rands/drbg.c#L200-L212

And if `drbg->parent_get_seed == NULL` it would fail. Is my reasoning correct?

As far as I understand it, things are actually quite the other way around: the get_entropy calls are the interface which was originally designed by NIST SP 800-90A for seeding and implemented that way in 1.1.1. Your upcall is deviating from that by 'misusing' the generate call, which causes your problems with low entropy seed sources. So imho #22342 doesn't fix the problem, just a symptom. It's better to fix it properly in 3.2 instead of waiting until people start writing independent entropy providers and need to implement workarounds.

issue_context.title: test/drgbtest fails for entropy factors other than 1 (VMS on Alpha, but not only)
issue_context.body:
Running `mms test /MAC=(TESTS="test_rand",V=1)` reveals this:

```
    # ERROR: (bool) 'EVP_RAND_instantiate(x, 0, 0, NULL, 0, NULL) == true' failed @ USER:[LEVITTE.TEST.openssl-3_2_0-alpha3-dev.test]drbgtest.c;2:820
    # false
    # 80CEAF7B00000000:error:1200007D:random number generator:(unknown function):random pool overflow:USER:[LEVITTE.TEST.openssl-3_2_0-alpha3-dev.crypto.rand]rand_pool.c;2:252:
    # 80CEAF7B00000000:error:030000D6:digital envelope routines:(unknown function):generate error:USER:[LEVITTE.TEST.openssl-3_2_0-alpha3-dev.crypto.evp]evp_rand.c;2:560:
    # 80CEAF7B00000000:error:1C8000BD:Provider routines:(unknown function):error retrieving entropy:USER:[LEVITTE.TEST.openssl-3_2_0-alpha3-dev.providers.implementations.rands]drbg.c;2:449:


pipe MCR dsa10:[axp.perl-5_20.][000000]perl.exe;1 [--.util]wrap.pl MCR [--.test]drbgtest.exe => 2
```
comments:
I applied a diff to find out a bit more:

``` diff
diff --git a/crypto/rand/rand_pool.c b/crypto/rand/rand_pool.c
index 8dc230b540..a5d5798e3b 100644
--- a/crypto/rand/rand_pool.c
+++ b/crypto/rand/rand_pool.c
@@ -249,7 +249,11 @@ size_t ossl_rand_pool_bytes_needed(RAND_POOL *pool, unsigned int entropy_factor)
 
     if (bytes_needed > pool->max_len - pool->len) {
         /* not enough space left */
-        ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_RAND, RAND_R_RANDOM_POOL_OVERFLOW);
+        ERR_raise_data(ERR_LIB_RAND, RAND_R_RANDOM_POOL_OVERFLOW,
+                       "entropy_factor=%u,entropy_needed=%zu,bytes_needed=%zu,"
+                       "pool->max_len=%zu,pool->len=%zu",
+                       entropy_factor, entropy_needed, bytes_needed,
+                       pool->max_len, pool->len);
         return 0;
     }
 
```

With that, the output tells me a little more:

```
    # 80CEAF7B00000000:error:1200007D:random number generator:(unknown function):random pool overflow:USER:[LEVITTE.TEST.openssl-3_2_0-alpha3-dev.crypto.rand]rand_pool.c;3:252:entropy_factor=20,entropy_needed=256,bytes_needed=640,pool->max_len=32,pool->len=0
```

The entropy factor indicates that we're using a lousy entropy gatherer, which is our fallback on VMS when the system service `SYS$GET_ENTROPY` isn't present (it's fairly new, and as I recall, only available on IA64 and x86_64), with an assumed entropy factor of 1 bit of entropy per 20 bits of data.

These definitions in `include/crypto/rand_pool.h` make ample space for even that lousy gatherer:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2b8d81534479b161dda063477272363fb2caef08/include/crypto/rand_pool.h#L17-L41

However, `ossl_rand_pool_new()` allows a *smaller* customized max length, and it seems that at least some calls assume a much better entropy factor, and that's what causes this failure.

Not really sure what's the right thing to do with this.
Why we haven't seen this error earlier?  I frankly don't know, I haven't followed all the ins and outs surrounding rand and drbg...

There are implicit assumptions that the entropy being grabbed is full strength (i.e. 8 bits per byte).
I've been aware of this for a while now and wondered when we'd hit it.

Time to think...

The underlying assumption is the generate call which is assuming 8 bits per byte of entropy gets produced.  The seed source doesn't achieve this on all platform so the call fails due to insufficient space.
I might have found a more satisfying solution to the problem. Working on a patch...

review_comments: Not a public API (yet). Could be made public as `EVP_RAND_clear_seed()` in 3.2 and backported as non-public function.
We really should do something similar in the `ossl_rand_get_user_nonce()` as well.
This (fixing the nonce code as well) is still sensible I think and it's a straightforward change.

> We really should do something similar in the `ossl_rand_get_user_nonce()` as well.

I would have done it right from the beginning (you know I love consistency) and it would have been a straightforward change, if there hadn't been an awkward fracture in the API's consistency: 


This is the signature of the upcall:


```C
size_t ossl_rand_get_user_nonce(OSSL_LIB_CTX *ctx,
                                unsigned char **pout,
                                size_t min_len, size_t max_len,
                                const void *salt, size_t salt_len)
```

and the obvious implementation would have been

```C
size_t ossl_rand_get_user_nonce(OSSL_LIB_CTX *ctx,
                                unsigned char **pout,
                                size_t min_len, size_t max_len,
                                const void *salt, size_t salt_len)
{
   EVP_RAND_CTX *rng = ossl_rand_get0_seed_noncreating(ctx);

    if (rng != NULL && evp_rand_has_nonce(rng))
        return evp_rand_get_nonce(rng, pout, min_len, max_len, salt, salt_len);
    else
        return ossl_rand_get_nonce(ctx, pout, min_len, max_len, salt, salt_len);
}
```
analogous to the user seed implementation.

However, instead of a pair `rand_get_nonce`/`rand_clear_nonce` where the callee allocates and cleans up the memory,


```C
OSSL_CORE_MAKE_FUNC(size_t,rand_get_nonce,
                    (void *vctx, unsigned char **buffer,
                     size_t min_len, size_t max_len,
                     const void *salt, size_t salt_len))
OSSL_CORE_MAKE_FUNC(void,rand_clear_nonce,
                    (void *vctx, unsigned char *buffer, size_t b_len))
```

there is a only a method

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/fac61ea4618c83826b51aebf03cbc2bc3ac7b8c8/include/openssl/core_dispatch.h#L492-L494

which is expected to be called twice, the first time with a NULL buffer to determine the the length of the buffer to be allocated by the caller (note the `unsigned char *out` instead of `unsigned char **pout`). Also, the `salt` and `salt_len` is missing from the arguments.

And that fracture is not easy to fix, because the method is public as `EVP_RAND_nonce()`. :-/
see also https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/22394#pullrequestreview-1678916810.

`ossl_rand_get_user_nonce()` hasn't been in a release and is consequently mutable at least until later today.  Although you're not proposing a change so it might be okay even so.

More over, `ossl_rand_get_user_nonce()` is only ever called by the FIPS provider (and similar 3rd party providers) which will never call `EVP_RAND_nonce()`, so again it should be okay.

Finally, we don't call `EVP_RAND_nonce()` anywhere and implementing it (very) inefficiently might be acceptable.  It currently, even after this proposal, will never hit `ossl_rand_get_user_nonce()`.  It tries to call the nonce method and falls back to the generate method if it isn't present.  I.e. it will work the same with or without this change.
I did not fully understand you answer. Maybe we can talk about this briefly at the end of our OTC meeting?
Or before??

Essentially, `EVP_RAND_nonce()` is independent of `ossl_rand_get_user_nonce()`.  The API difference doesn't matter IMO.

The first is a call to an EVP_RAND to generate some data.  Typically a DRBG but it could be an entropy source.

The second is a provider to libcrypto call to collect some data which is used to seed the DRBGs.   It's called from [`ossl_prov_get_nonce()`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/fac61ea4618c83826b51aebf03cbc2bc3ac7b8c8/providers/common/provider_seeding.c#L105) in provider_seeding.c on the provider side which is called from [`prov_drbg_get_nonce()`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/fac61ea4618c83826b51aebf03cbc2bc3ac7b8c8/providers/implementations/rands/drbg.c#L305) in drbg.c which in turn is called from [`ossl_prov_drbg_instantiate()`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/fac61ea4618c83826b51aebf03cbc2bc3ac7b8c8/providers/implementations/rands/drbg.c#L425-L433) if a DRBG has no parent.  It should only be called from the FIPS provider since that's the only place a DRBG doesn't end up with a parent.  Of course, third party providers have probably done a copy paste and end up calling it too.

> Or before??

_(That was not possible due to another meeting)_
@paulidale and I (and others) had a talk and I'll come with a proposal within the next days.

Should we retain this code path for the case where `rng != NULL && !evp_rand_can_seed(rng)` ?  Existing seed sources are not going to support the new callbacks and will devolve to the current behaviour of gathering entropy themselves.  Fixing that was primary intent behind the earlier change.

> Should we retain this code path for the case where `rng != NULL && !evp_rand_can_seed(rng)` ? Existing seed sources are not going to support the new callbacks and will devolve to the current behaviour of gathering entropy themselves.

I thought about that option as well and discarded it. In view of what I wrote in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/22394#issuecomment-1774773581 it is not necessary to 'fix' the case where the seed source doesn't implement the get_entropy hooks. It just makes things more convoluted.

>  Fixing that was primary intent behind the earlier change.

The intention was to fix the VMS low entropy seeding problem, which this pull request achieves as well.

I'm not sure this is worthwhile.  It's not going to hurt but it might be better pre-pended/appended to the pool and processed via the DRBG seeding mechanics.

I couldn't think of any other way to use the additional input in my flawed fix.
Ditch this line?
We usually don't put an else after a return but it's not a big deal.
Not a public API (yet). Could be made public as `EVP_RAND_get_seed()` in 3.2 and backported as non-public function.

Wasn't intended to be EVP visible but the underlying calls are part of our public provider API.

I think there are a number of risks associated with making this public.  Chief among them, misuse of the material.
Ok, agreed. But why is ~~`EVP_rand()`~~ `EVP_RAND_nonce()`  public and `EVP_RAND_get_seed()` not?

`EVP_RAND()`?? It's a type not a function.

The seeding is internal to the DRBGs -- never called by anything else.  The DRBG's know about a few of their parent's calls and go direct so that they can support cross provider chaining.

At least before this PR it was internal.
Sorry, I meant to write `EVP_RAND_nonce()`.
A check that either none or both of these are defined should be included in the block below.
